evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep said: 'we just need to ask you some information or est in order for us to build you an accurate code. You can depend on this would take within the next fifteen to ten to fifteen minutes of your time. Would that be okay?' — framing present but rushed past without genuine pause; customer says 'Okay' but conversation flows immediately into name-collection without waiting for real affirmation.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep moves directly from initial details into logistics probing (floor, dimensions, walk distance, special items) without asking 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?'
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no concerns volunteered by customer during Section 2 window. Customer's objection ('500 is way too much') surfaces only during Section 4 estimate discussion, outside the Section 2 concern-gathering frame.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no concerns raised in Section 2 to reflect back.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Partial. Covered: storage unit floor (first floor, indoor), dimensions (10x10x8), fill level (75%), walk distance (30 feet), special items (heavy desk in box, ceramic dishes container, decorations). Missing/unclear: property type at destination (stated 'house' + 'garage attached' but not probed for stories/rooms), additional stops (none mentioned, appears to be two-stop only). Storage unit details covered well; destination property details minimal.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Yes. Rep asked 'do you happen to know how many boxes are we moving?' Customer responded 'If I say fifty maybe' — rep confirmed 'Fifty boxes.'
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: No. Rep never asked 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?' — logical since items already packed, but not offered or explicitly declined.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Partial. Rep gave range ('two and a half to three and a half hours estimated cost would be $662 to $782') anchored to typical 10x10 unit time, but personalization was weak — rep acknowledged 'we are only moving the items that you have provided' and 'short distance' but did not tie estimate to customer's stated concerns (tight budget, broken arm, cost objection) or explicitly state why the range applies to this move's specifics.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full. Rep disclosed: hourly rate ($101/hour per mover), what's included (truck, gas, taxes, insurance, wraps, tools), no hidden fees (no credit card fees, sterile fees, disassemble/assembly fees), minimum 2.5 hours, 15-minute increments beyond minimum. Stated: 'there's no hidden fees of any type.'
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. After giving estimate ($662–$782), rep immediately pivoted to availability ('upon checking here on the thirteenth') without asking 'Does that feel fair?' and holding silence.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Full. Rep stated: 'we have on time guarantee we value your time. So, if you cannot make it to the time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill.'
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Partial. Rep stated: 'we have no worry damage coverage included on the R-D weight that you're paying us. We will provide up to 2000 dollars per move that is to repair replace and members for your items.' — covers the $2,000 limit and that it's included, but did not explicitly state 'no deductible' or 'no fine print' framing as the rubric requires.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: False. Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or confirm customer acceptance of the two promises before moving on. Conversation flows into availability/booking without closure on promises section.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Rep never asks a genuine version of 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or even a throwaway 'Any questions?' before or after the estimate discussion. Customer volunteers objection ('500 is way too much') unprompted during estimate clarification, but rep does not return to a final concerns check after that.
evidence_quotes.followup_on_remaining_concern: N/A — no concern raised in Section 6 window. Customer's price objection occurs during Section 4 estimate discussion and is not followed up; call ends without addressing it.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: False. Rep never asks 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never. Rep never asks 'Would you like our help with your move?' or any recognizable version of an explicit ask for the business. When customer objects to price, rep does not pivot to an ask — call simply ends.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: False. Rep mentions 'no deposit required' and 'no rest secure in your spot' but does not mention rate-lock or assurance that the price won't change if customer books now.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Rep confirmed: date (October 13, second week), arrival window (8:30 AM–9:00 AM), no deposit required, reschedule/cancel flexibility, phone number to call. Missing: phone number for customer confirmation (rep provided Einstein's number to call, not customer's phone taken), crew size confirmed (two movers), addresses re-confirmed (storage and home stated, not re-read back to close), notes left for crew (none documented). Call ends before booking is completed — customer objects to price and conversation terminates without confirmation of a booking.

top_strength: Rep gathered comprehensive storage and logistics details efficiently, asked about box count, and delivered full pricing-structure transparency including hourly rate, inclusions, no hidden fees, and the 2.5-hour minimum with 15-minute increments.
coaching_note: Never ask for the business or close the loop on concerns — skip 'Their Agenda' entirely, don't hold silence after pricing, miss the final concerns check, and the call ends with the customer objecting to cost and walking away unaddressed.
